scope: Bedside lung ultrasound signs in critical illness.

keyRecommendations.text: A-lines are horizontal repetitions of the pleural line and indicate gas.
Lung sliding is a to-and-fro movement at the pleural line; M-mode shows the seashore sign and indicates that the visceral pleura is included.
In the BLUE protocol, only anterolateral lung rockets are used, because posterior interstitial changes can be due to gravity.

clinicalBottomLine: Thoracic ultrasound in this review is a pattern of signs: gas (A-lines), sliding pleura, interstitial rockets, effusion (quad and sinusoid signs), and consolidation (fractal and tissue-like signs).
notableCaveats: This is a critical-care ultrasound review, not a radiology curriculum for every thoracic indication.
